title: A paused task renders as "Blocked," a false signal that draws intervention nothing needs
description:
Reported by lore-cli (routed via opum-agent), observed directly against its own tracker: LCLI-487 read status "Blocked" after lore-cli ran quest task pause to park it cleanly with its investigation written up -- nothing was actually blocking it. Root cause is structural, not a one-off misconfiguration: quest-cli own status flow (this repository quest task status-flow) configures pausedStatus as "Blocked", and quest instructions task-finalization documents this as the default ("quest task pause <id> parks it at the configured paused status (\"Blocked\" by default)"). There is no In Progress -> To Do transition, so task pause is the only way out of In Progress, and it lands on the same status name every session in this fleet is trained to read as "needs intervention" -- exactly what a session escalates on and what an orchestrator goes looking at. A status that says a human is needed when none is costs the attention the genuinely blocked tasks need.

This task records the observed harm; it does not prescribe the fix. At least two shapes were named when this was routed: (a) a real In Progress -> To Do transition, so pausing cleanly-parked work does not require reusing the blocked status at all, or (b) a paused status distinct from blocked in the default status flow. Picking between them, or another shape, or declining to change anything, is a product decision for whoever works this task -- not decided here.

acceptanceCriteria.text: A decision is made and recorded among at least the two named shapes (a real In Progress -> To Do transition; a paused status distinct from Blocked) or another shape, with reasoning -- or an explicit reason to leave current behavior unchanged
If a change is chosen, it is implemented and demonstrated: pausing a task that is not actually blocked no longer reports a status a session or orchestrator would read as needing intervention
The chosen behavior (changed or deliberately kept) is documented in the relevant quest instructions guide so a session reading a paused task status is not misled again

plan: 1. Confirmed pausedStatus is not workspace-configurable and no task in .quest/tasks currently sits at status Blocked

2. Chose shape (b): rename defaultLifecyclePolicy.pausedStatus from Blocked to Paused in src/domain/tasks/tasks.ts, keeping pausedStatus structurally separate from the statuses ladder built by QCLI-229, rather than shape (a) adding an In Progress to To Do ladder edge, which would collapse pause into a demotion and lose the started-not-reset semantics

3. Propagate the literal rename to src/contract/tracker/fixtures.ts, src/application/command-help.ts, src/application/agents/guides.ts (task-finalization guide text, satisfies AC3), and the tests asserting the default pausedStatus value in tasks.test.ts and cli-semantics.test.ts
implementationNotes: Chose shape (b): renamed defaultLifecyclePolicy.pausedStatus from "Blocked" to "Paused" in src/domain/tasks/tasks.ts, rather than shape (a) adding a real In Progress to To Do ladder transition. pauseTask/startTask/legalDemoteTargets/demoteTask deliberately keep pausedStatus structurally separate from the statuses ladder (QCLI-229), specifically so pausing records that work was started rather than resetting it -- collapsing pause into a To Do ladder edge would destroy that distinction on purpose built by QCLI-229. Renaming the string is the narrow, structure-preserving fix.

Propagated the literal rename to src/contract/tracker/fixtures.ts (conformance fixture), src/application/command-help.ts (task pause help text), src/application/agents/guides.ts (task-finalization guide text, satisfies AC3), and the tests asserting the default value: test/integration/tasks/tasks.test.ts and test/integration/tasks/cli-semantics.test.ts. Deliberately left docs/reference/quest-cli-release-truth.md untouched (dated 0.4.0/QCLI-229 release history) and left test/integration/tasks/tasks.test.ts:628 unchanged (an arbitrary invalid-status example unrelated to pausedStatus). Also left several docs/*.md and test/cli-tracker-process.test.ts Blocked matches untouched after confirming they are unrelated: decision-record status Blocked, a Blocked-by table column header, git log entries, and task titles used to test dependency-based readiness filtering.

Verified with bun run check (fully green: 482 pass, 0 fail, 4185 expect() calls across 56 files) and with a direct manual run against runQuest (src/cli/main.ts) on a scratch store: create -> edit --status "In Progress" -> pause returned {"kind":"task.paused","data":{"status":"Paused"}} with exitCode 0; task view and task status-flow both echoed "Paused"; task start returned it to "In Progress". This is genuine evidence for AC2, not just unit-test coverage. Confirmed no task in this repository own .quest/tasks currently sits at status "Blocked" via grep -l "\"status\":\"Blocked\"" .quest/tasks/*.json (zero matches), so this rename has no in-repo migration concern.

Worth a release-notes line, not a new task per this task own scope: any other Opum-fleet Quest workspace that currently has a task parked at status "Blocked" (the old default pausedStatus) will, after this ships, no longer have that literal string recognized by quest task start as "the paused status" -- pauseTask/startTask/legalDemoteTargets/demoteTask all compare against the configured pausedStatus value by exact string, so an existing "Blocked" task becomes an ordinary, unrecognized status string post-upgrade rather than being auto-migrated to "Paused." lore-cli own tracker (which reported this via LCLI-487) is one plausible instance to check.
finalSummary: Renamed the default pausedStatus from "Blocked" to "Paused" (shape b), keeping the paused status structurally separate from the statuses ladder that QCLI-229 built on purpose, rather than collapsing pause into a new In Progress -> To Do ladder edge (shape a). Changed src/domain/tasks/tasks.ts, src/contract/tracker/fixtures.ts, src/application/command-help.ts, src/application/agents/guides.ts (task-finalization guide text), and the tests asserting the default value. Verified with bun run check (482 pass, 0 fail) and a direct manual run against runQuest: pausing a freshly created, non-blocked task now returns {"kind":"task.paused","data":{"status":"Paused"}} instead of "Blocked". No task in this repository .quest/tasks currently sits at "Blocked", so there is no in-repo migration to perform, but other fleet workspaces with a task parked at "Blocked" will need a release-notes callout -- recorded in the implementation notes rather than filed as a new task, per instructions.
